summary: Daijo Tokiwa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1896 to 1899 and held a post at Toyo University from circa 1901 to 1939.

Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. In 2015, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at Taisho University and as a full-time lecturer of sectarian studies at Chisan Denpoin.

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and under traditional teacher Eko Hashimoto (~1946–1953). He taught Taigen Dan Leighton and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda University, the University of Tokyo, and under Kosen Imakita, Soen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He held posts at Otani University, Columbia University, and Matsugaoka Bunko.

Daishun Ueyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He served at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor (attested 1972–1973) and as president in 1983.

Dale S. Wright works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann, and became the David B. and Mary H. Gamble Professor at Occidental College around 1979.

Dalsukh D. Malvania was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1951) and served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1965–1971).
Damdin Badaraev is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidya Dandaron and George Roerich.

Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford, and became Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London, around 1990.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Cambridge Rindge and Latin School, Harvard University, and Fergusson College, and held a post at Banaras Hindu University circa 1930–1931.

Dan Arnold specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College, Iliff School of Theology, and the University of Chicago under multiple teachers, he held posts at McGill University, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and University of Chicago.

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Temple University, studying under scholars including Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Grinnell, Macalester, Florida State, Georgia, Harvard, Bates, UCLA, UIUC, and Boston University.

Dan Martin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yonten Gyatso, Cheojey Lama, Gelek Rimpoche, and Elliot Sperling at Indiana University (Ph.D. ~1984–1991), and held posts at Hebrew University, Carnegie Mellon, and the Norwegian Academy.

Dan Smyer Yü is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of California, Davis, and served as Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who completed his PhD at KU Leuven (~1990–1994) and his Habilitation at the University of Copenhagen (~1995–1999). Around 2002, he became Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Center for Subjectivity Research there.

Daniel A. Getz is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, Ying-shih Yü, Masaaki Chikusa, and Tairyo Makita. He was an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).

Daniel Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under the supervision of Jay L. Garfield, and also studied under Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who earned his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He held posts at Butler University (attested 1986), the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and Soka University.
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley (attested 2014).
